{{Top|leg}}
{{Youmay|the general concept of magic in [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]]|the [[magick]]s used by the [[Nightsisters]] in [[canon]]}}
[[File:Morag_and_Umwak.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Umwak]] the [[Dulok/Legends|Dulok]] [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]] and [[Morag]] the [[Tulgah/Legends|Tulgah]] witch]]
{{Quote|It's not the Force, it's magic!|[[Adler Roty]]|<ref name="HNN">[[HoloNet News (original website)|''HoloNet News'' website]]</ref>}}
'''Magic''' was a catch-all term referring to any of a number of supernatural techniques or occult teachings outside of conventional [[The Force/Legends|Force]] [[Force power/Legends|powers]]. It was thought that magic allowed sorcerous practitioners to conjure and wield great powers or to manipulate aspects of reality in order to influence events.<ref name="BoS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

==Description==
{{Quote|Magic is an art of patience. The study of the natural ways involves many years of the strictest devotion. Terrible things can happen to a young wizard who foolishly misuses his knowledge.|[[Logray/Legends|Logray]] to [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo]]|<ref name="ShadowStone">''[[The Shadow Stone: An Ewok Adventure]]''</ref>}}
The exact nature of magic remains in dispute among philosophers, as does its relationship to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] proper. It is possible that all "magic" traditions were simply different methods of accessing the same Force, or were emanations of different aspects of it. More so than the Force, magic potency could be trapped in artifacts or locations&mdash;but again, this may be just due to different methods of accessing and using the Force.

The term was also sometimes mistakenly used by primitives or less-informed people to refer to the Force powers of mainstream [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], who were likely to be called "wizards" and their abilities attributed to "magic." The [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] for example referred to [[Revan/Legends|Revan's]] powers as magic, much to the dismay of Revan, who tried to explain the difference to them. [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] also referred to [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi's]] powers as "magic." Similarly, [[Owen Lars]] described Kenobi as a "wizard", while [[Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti|Motti]] derisively compared [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader's]] "sorcerer's ways" to feats traditionally attributed to magic. 

Derivatives of the word "magic" and words such as "[[Witch/Legends|witch]]" are terms describing [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] users or powers ([[Witches of Dathomir]], [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]], [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]], [[Morag]] identified as "Witch," [[Prophets of the Dark Side|Emperor's Mage]]) which had almost exclusively negative connotations.

The [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]], for example, were "crafters" of various [[Spirit (Nightsisters)|spirit]]-willed [[Dathomir Magic|magics]], with the [[Shaman of the Nightsisters|shaman]] and clan leader [[Mother (title)/Legends|Mother]] [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]] being the most powerful of the magic-wielding witches. Methods of channeling energies of the Nightsisters' [[Daughter/Legends|Winged Goddess]] or [[Son/Legends|Fanged God]] included conjuring objects from raw [[Spirit ichor/Legends|spirit ichor]], divination ([[heartshadow]]), scrying, spell-casting or incantation, [[mesmerism]], ur-spirit communication, spirit-infusion of [[Talisman (artifact)|talismans]] and [[totem]]s, and spirit-conjuring techniques linked with Nature.<ref name="BoS" /> Some Jedi also used Dathomir magic.<ref name="Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen">''[[Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen]]''</ref>

Finally, magic also referred to the non-supernatural stage trickery of entertainers like [[Wim Magwit]].

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|It will be like magic, young Anakin Skywalker.''"<br />"''I don't need magic," Anakin said solemnly.<br />Shappa laughed a little nervously. "Neither do you, I bet," he said to Obi-Wan. Obi-Wan smiled.<br />"I forgot. You're Jedi. No magic, then. But of mystery there will be plenty...|[[Zonama Sekot/Legends|Zonama Sekot]] sentient ship designer [[Shappa Farrs]] asks [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], in [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]], to join with him in the design of their unique and personalized living [[Sekotan Personal Starship|Sekotan starship]], the ''[[Jabitha]]''|<ref name="Rogue Planet">''[[Rogue Planet]]''</ref>}}
The use of real-life occult terms (witch, mage, prophet, warlock, alchemy, cult) almost exclusively to refer to Sith organizations or entities creates a parallel between an orthodox religion (the Jedi) and a cult or breakaway faction (the Sith).

In [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game|''Star Wars'' roleplaying games]], [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]] have the role of magic spells of traditional fantasy RPGs. The [[Personal Force reservoir|Force repository]] is also comparable to the "mana pool" of fantasy games.

A connection of fantasy magic and the Force has been "attempted" during an April Fools' joke which wanted the [[Midi-chlorian/Legends|midi-chlorians]] originate from the "planet [[Andowyne]]," the fantasy world of [[Willow (film)|''Willow'']].
